mission_requirements.text: The EPS engineering enterprise shall obtain MCR acceptance at the end of Pre-Phase A for a mission concept whose EPS feasibility is justified against agreed stakeholder expectations and mission constraints, supported by initial ConOps, budgets, assumptions, risks and a preliminary verification and validation approach.

The enterprise shall obtain SRR acceptance during Phase A for validated EPS requirements and interfaces traced to the mission concept and allocated spacecraft requirements, with measurable criteria consistent with stakeholder expectations. It shall derive, refine and validate EPS and component requirements and interfaces as the design matures through Phase B and adapted C.

The enterprise shall obtain MDR/SDR acceptance at the end of Phase A for a credible EPS architecture with requirement allocations and justified alternatives, and PDR acceptance at the end of Phase B for a sized, compatible preliminary design supported by sizing and trades, margins, risk dispositions, controlled interfaces and verification and validation plans against applicable requirements and agreed resource and risk limits.

The enterprise shall obtain CDR acceptance during adapted Phase C, before deliverable coding, for complete detailed EPS model/software design, interface specifications and implementation, integration and verification and validation plans, followed by SIR acceptance at the end of C for released models and declared host-executed control/interface software, applicable MIL/SIL evidence, compatible interfaces and ready integration configurations and procedures.

The enterprise shall establish and maintain coherent phase baselines through authorized changes, repeated affected checks and applicable verification and validation evidence, retaining configuration-linked requirements, expectations, methods, results, limitations and finding dispositions. It shall obtain and retain acceptance decisions from the designated review authority against agreed success criteria, prevent progression with blocking findings, and record conditional limits, closure actions, owners and dates.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain each requirement with its identifier, revision, statement, product level, source and parent revisions, rationale, owner, conditions or quantities, applicable units, verification method, criterion and resolution status, including reasons for unresolved or inapplicable fields.

The framework shall check created or edited requirement drafts on each edit or request for declared deterministic quality errors, probable semantic duplicates, coverage gaps and source conflicts, returning affected text or records, the rule or cited passage, corrective suggestions or questions, uncertainty and assessment limits.

The framework shall recommend derivation, analysis, verification and validation methods or models on edits or requests using the current lifecycle stage, engineering question, requirements, available inputs, validity, resources and scope, with applicability conditions, rationale, cited sources, alternatives and rejection records.

The framework shall retrieve forward and reverse links among expectations, ConOps scenarios, requirements, function and element allocations, interfaces, decisions and applicable evidence, reporting missing or ambiguous endpoints and coverage against the declared reference set.

The framework shall identify reciprocal impacts of a proposed mission, requirement, component, interface, model or software change on EPS/non-EPS allocations, budgets, trades, plans, guidance and evidence, reporting unresolved dependencies and required reassessments.

The framework shall issue a distinct successor baseline only for an authorized engineering change decision, preserving its predecessor, request, rationale, findings and dispositions and identifying regenerated, stale and unresolved products and evidence.

The framework shall retain retrievable phase baselines that resolve exact requirement, mission, design, model, software, interface and evidence revisions with revision history and the authorized decisions that control them.

The framework shall check transferred identities, revisions, structure, quantities, units, polarity, time/mode meanings and provenance against the declared interface specification before registration, retaining incompatible raw submissions and findings without replacing controlled content.

The framework shall associate each analysis or software result with its requirement/expectation, method, scenario, design/model/software/input revisions, parameters, producer, execution environment, raw outputs, logs and execution status, preserving failed, cancelled and partial runs.

The framework shall provide the controlled inputs, dependencies and instructions to reconstruct a designated analysis or MIL/SIL run and compare its raw outputs using result-specific rules and tolerances fixed before replay, retaining comparison failures and missing dependencies.

The framework shall report missing, rejected, stale, failed, out-of-domain and unresolved evidence against the affected requirements, expectations and conclusions with criticality, owner and disposition, preventing unqualified current conformity claims from affected critical gaps.

The framework shall generate and revise candidate-specific bills of materials from modeled design occurrences with assembly relationships, quantities, part and variant identifiers, source revisions and selection status.

The framework shall calculate revision-linked EPS mass, volume and acquisition-cost estimates from the bill of materials and declared additional categories, retaining sources, price dates, currencies, availability assumptions, uncertainty and unknown values.

The framework shall compare designated EPS concepts and architectures on common requirements, mission assumptions and engineer-approved criteria, separating mandatory feasibility from preference ranking and reporting raw measures, margins, uncertainty, sensitivity, risks and selection rationale.

The framework shall configure EPS design representations through identified parameters, component variants and extensions covering generation, storage, conversion, regulation, protection, distribution, control, interfaces and requirement allocations.

The framework shall compose time-dependent subsystem loads, schedules and mode transitions with orbit, attitude, illumination, eclipse, thermal conditions and modeled EPS generation, storage, losses and protection to report power/energy balance, bus quantities and battery state within the declared model scope.

The framework shall produce proposed EPS and component requirement allocations from identified spacecraft requirements, scenarios and sourced design quantities using a declared derivation method, retaining parent links, units, assumptions, uncertainty and engineer dispositions.

The framework shall exchange identified component and design models with declared electrical, thermal, applicable EMC and geometry analysis profiles, retaining input/output mappings, tool versions, units, supported effects and unsupported or lossy transfers.

The framework shall coordinate MIL assessment of modeled EPS control against the plant and mission scenarios for nominal operation, load/supply changes, mode transitions, selected faults, protection and recovery, retaining stimuli, expected/actual responses, criteria and failures.

The framework shall calculate preliminary generation, demand and energy budgets and array/battery sizing for the declared mission modes, including sourced efficiencies, duty cycles, eclipse duration, allowable battery operating limits, degradation assumptions and engineer-defined margins.

The framework shall associate each model-supported conclusion with intended use, selected fidelity, included and omitted mechanisms, numerical checks, validity domain, uncertainty, calibration evidence and independent assessment evidence or explicit gaps, with engineer-approved prediction-error rules.

The framework shall propose identified model calibration or parameter revisions from quality-checked supplied reference data, retaining prior/revised values, data revisions, residuals, uncertainty and affected analyses separately from independent model assessment.

The framework shall retain the fidelity, solver and coupling configuration, time step, convergence rules, execution environment, required resources and estimated/measured runtime for each analysis, MIL or SIL run, with unmet resource or numerical limits reported.

The framework shall coordinate SIL assessment of the declared host-executed control/interface code with simulated EPS and subsystem products, reporting requirement/ConOps outcomes and differences from corresponding MIL results for the same scenarios and comparison rules.

The framework shall retain mission expectations, constraints and nominal/degraded ConOps scenarios with orbit, attitude, duration, environmental conditions, subsystem modes, load schedules and transitions as revision-linked inputs to EPS requirements and analysis.

The framework shall identify reliability, availability and maintainability analyses applicable to the designated EPS requirements, ConOps and risks, retaining the chosen measures, failure/repair assumptions, method coverage and reasons for exclusions.

The framework shall generate the selected RAM analysis representation from identified functions, components and failure dependencies using declared transformation rules, preserving sourced or missing failure/repair data and uncertainty in the reported results.

The framework shall retain EPS phase-product verification and validation plans with distinct requirement and expectation/ConOps references, subject configuration, method, conditions, inputs, expected response, criteria, observations, applicability limits and planned/executed status.

The framework shall retain the authorized engineer disposition of each requirement correction or method/model suggestion as accepted, modified, rejected or deferred, with rationale and the exact suggestion and context revisions.

The framework shall mark affected assistance stale when its requirement, mission, design, source, criterion or scope revision changes, prevent stale suggestions from being applied as current guidance and initiate reassessment for the new context.

The framework shall retain scenario time bases, sample and receipt times, sampling, synchronization and known calculation/interface delays for simulated or supplied reference histories used in comparisons.

The framework shall check simulated and supplied reference histories for channel identity, units, timing, completeness and validity, preserving raw values, invalid samples, missing intervals and processing masks without treating missing or inactive readings as zero.

The framework shall retain revision-linked modeled EPS interfaces and command, telemetry, event and parameter definitions with endpoint ownership, identifiers, types, units, ranges, polarity, time/mode meaning and encodings.

The framework shall produce or coordinate checked mappings of the EPS interface specification to the engineer-selected host software integration profile, identifying version compatibility, unsupported behavior and lossy translations.

The framework shall specify and check modeled EPS command preconditions, order, effects, rejection/failure behavior, mode transitions, protection and recovery responsibilities against the declared control and interface requirements.

The framework shall coordinate coding and building of declared control/interface software through an external host execution toolchain only from an engineer-authorized detailed design release, retaining source/build revisions, dependencies, host configuration, logs and failures.

The framework shall generate filtered mission, requirement-allocation, design, interface and analysis views from controlled EPS records with baseline identification, readable units, legends and links to represented records.

The framework shall assemble a phase-baseline review package against the designated MCR, SRR, MDR/SDR, PDR, scoped CDR or scoped SIR entrance and success criteria, including applicable coverage, decisions, design, evidence, model limits, risks, gaps and finding dispositions.

The framework shall propose next engineering activities and repeated assessments from the declared phase, product maturity, dependencies, open findings and review criteria, identifying unmet prerequisites and the rationale for each proposal.

The framework shall acknowledge each assistance trigger and return a finding, recommendation or explicit pending/unavailable status within the engineer-approved interactive response limits, recording trigger, first-response and completion times for the current context.

The framework shall record a technical review disposition only from the designated authorized review authority against the identified baseline and agreed scoped success criteria, distinguishing prepared, accepted, conditional and progression-blocked status with rationale, conditions, closure actions, owners and dates.

measures_of_effectiveness.observation_basis: Engineering burden: active person-hours and elapsed hours for correct requirements, design, change and review tasks, with waiting and unattended execution reported separately.
Early issue detection: expert-confirmed issues found before scoped final design, critical misses and unnecessary investigations against a declared reference issue set.
Evidence and review usefulness: applicable requirement and expectation coverage, critical review defects, reviewer interpretation accuracy and successful independent reconstruction.
Adoption and affordability: person-hours to learn and complete correct tasks and adapt to a mission, and direct framework usage cost in CAD over a declared period and price date.
